documents.title: Pregnancy Confirmation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
G2P1, LMP 11/29/2024, about 5.5 weeks. First baby 4.5 months old, weaning now. Unplanned but welcome. Some nausea mornings. No bleeding.
Sugars less predictable over the holidays; already talked to endocrinology, appointment later this month.
Meds: glargine 22 u qHS, lispro 1:10, levothyroxine 75 mcg, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

Exam: vitals as charted, well. Urine hCG positive.

A/P
1. Pregnancy, second, with pre-existing T1DM: referral back to her obstetrics group placed.
2. A1c and TSH today.
3. Continue prenatal vitamin and levothyroxine 75 mcg.
Call with any severe lows or vomiting.

documents.body: Ophthalmology, 03/06/2025. Pregnant (about 14 weeks), type 1 diabetes. Vision 20/20 right, 20/20 left. Dilated fundus: no retinopathy, no edema. Plan routine annual follow-up. Allergies: none known.

documents.title: Endocrinology visit in pregnancy
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology, 04/08/2025, about 19 weeks.
This pregnancy has been harder than her first. Her log shows frequent high readings after meals and frequent lows, including two overnight lows that woke her. Adherent to insulin and to prenatal care; caring for an infant and teaching full time.
Insulin on the list unchanged: glargine 22 units at bedtime, lispro 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate; reviewed timing of meal doses, pre-bolusing and bedtime snack.
Weekly glucose reviews with our educator. NKDA. Levothyroxine 75 mcg, prenatal vitamin.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
~22.5 weeks, G2. Here mostly for thyroid and to touch base.

S: Sugars swinging both ways: highs after lunch at school, lows overnight and late afternoon. Endocrinology reviewing her log weekly; she is taking every dose and going to every OB visit. Exhausted with a 9-month-old. No vision change, no headaches, no swelling. Baby moving.
Meds: glargine 22 u qHS, lispro 1:10 with meals, levothyroxine 75 mcg, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

O: BP normal, vitals as charted. Gravid. No edema.

A/P
1. T1DM in pregnancy with labile glucose: managed by endocrinology and OB; A1c today, copy to both. Made sure she has glucose tabs at school and by the bed.
2. Hypothyroidism: TSH today, 75 mcg.
3. Tdap at OB around 28 weeks.
Text me if things get harder.

documents.title: Obstetrics visit note
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body: Obstetrics prenatal visit 06/20/2025, 29 weeks. Tdap administered, right deltoid. Fetal heart tones normal. Glucose control remains difficult per endocrinology; continued co-management. NKDA.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: hospital obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 08/30/2025, discharged 09/01/2025.

29-year-old G2P1 at 39 weeks 1 day in active labor, a year after her first vaginal delivery. Type 1 diabetes and autoimmune hypothyroidism. Glucose was difficult to control throughout this pregnancy, with frequent hyperglycemia and frequent hypoglycemia, despite consistent insulin use and full attendance at prenatal care. Prenatal course otherwise unremarkable.
Allergies: NKDA. Surgical history: none.
Home medications: insulin glargine 22 units subcut at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals, 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate; levothyroxine 75 mcg by mouth daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.

On arrival: uncomfortable with contractions, in moderate distress during them. Vital signs stable. Fetal tracing reassuring. Cervix 6 cm, 90% effaced.
Course: delivered by normal spontaneous vaginal delivery two hours after admission. Male infant, 4,500 g (macrosomic). Apgar 8 at 1 minute and 9 at 5 minutes.
Newborn: jittery and irritable at 30 minutes of life. Infant glucose 25 mg/dL; infant hemoglobin 17 g/dL; calcium 9.2 mg/dL; magnesium 2.1 mg/dL; CBC otherwise unremarkable. Neonatal hypoglycemia, managed by the newborn team.
Mother: postpartum course uncomplicated; insulin back to home doses with endocrinology input.

Diagnoses (maternal): term pregnancy, delivered; normal spontaneous vaginal delivery; type 1 diabetes with poor control during pregnancy; hypothyroidism.
Discharge medications: unchanged from home.
Follow-up: obstetrics 6 weeks, endocrinology 1-2 weeks, primary care.

documents.title: Postpartum Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
2.5 weeks after second vaginal delivery (8/30). Summary reviewed: big baby boy, 4,500 g, low blood sugar after birth handled by the newborn team; he is home and feeding well now per mom.

S: She is sore but recovering, bleeding tapering. Breastfeeding. Two under 13 months, tired. Sugars settled within days of delivery; endocrinology saw her and kept the usual doses. Mood: "overwhelmed some days, not sad." Has help from her mother.
Meds: glargine 22 u qHS, lispro 1:10, levothyroxine 75 mcg, prenatal vitamin. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted. Tired, appropriate. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen soft, fundus not felt. Legs without swelling or tenderness.
PHQ-9: 5.

A/P
1. Postpartum, uncomplicated maternal course: OB at 6 weeks.
2. T1DM: A1c, urine microalbumin, CMP, lipids today (yearly labs due).
3. Hypothyroidism: TSH.
4. Mood: mild, normal-range screen; reviewed warning signs. Will recheck at next visit.
Flu/COVID next month.

documents.title: Vaccines
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Flu vaccine and 2025-26 COVID vaccine, one in each arm. Back at school this week after leave. Nursing; reviewed both are fine. Waited 15 min.

documents.title: Endocrinology follow-up
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Endocrinology, 11/11/2025. About 10 weeks postpartum. Lability much less than in pregnancy. Mild lows a few times a week in the afternoon, self-treated.
Continue glargine 22 units at bedtime and lispro 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate. Levothyroxine 75 mcg. Discussed planning ahead of any further pregnancy.
NKDA. Follow-up 3 months.

documents.title: Positive again
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Positive test again. LMP October 27. I know. Can I come in next week? Already emailed endo.

documents.title: Re: Positive again
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Of course. You're booked Tuesday the 16th after school. Prenatal vitamin daily, and call endocrinology if the lows pick up.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
31 weeks, G3P2. Last week of classes before summer.

S: Feels well for the third trimester. Sugars steadier than last time; endocrinology every 2-3 weeks, no list changes. Baby active. Tdap done at OB last month. No headaches, visual change or swelling.
Meds: insulin glargine 22 u qHS, insulin lispro 1 u/10 g carb with meals, levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, prenatal vitamin with iron. NKDA.

O: vitals as charted, BP normal. Gravid, fundus above umbilicus. No edema. Mood bright.
PHQ-9: 3.

A/P
1. Hypothyroidism in pregnancy: TSH and free T4 today.
2. T1DM in pregnancy: A1c today, copies to OB and endo.
3. Delivery plan per obstetrics; she'll message after the baby comes and we will see her postpartum.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Maya, thyroid tests are in range, so the 75 mcg stays. A1c is in a good place for this point in pregnancy. Sent to obstetrics and endocrinology. Enjoy the start of summer.

documents.title: Levothyroxine refill

documents.body: Refill request levothyroxine 75 mcg, 90-day supply. TSH 6/2 in range. Approved per protocol.

documents.title: Obstetric discharge summary
documents.author: hospital obstetrics
documents.body:
Regional hospital, labor and delivery. Admitted 07/24/2026, discharged 07/27/2026.

30-year-old G3P2 at 38 weeks 4 days with type 1 diabetes and autoimmune hypothyroidism, admitted in labor. Prior vaginal deliveries in August 2024 and August 2025; the 2025 pregnancy had difficult glucose control and the infant had neonatal hypoglycemia.
Allergies: NKDA. Surgical history before this admission: none.
Home medications: insulin glargine 22 units at bedtime; insulin lispro with meals at 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate; levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; prenatal vitamin with iron daily.

Course: membranes ruptured spontaneously shortly after admission with a large amount of clear fluid. About 15 minutes later she felt something suddenly between her legs, became very anxious and noticed less fetal movement. Nursing noted the fetal heart rate, normal until then, fall to 70 beats per minute and stay there for more than a minute despite position changes and oxygen. Cervix 7 cm; a firm, pulsating cord felt alongside the presenting part, with the head high and poorly applied to the cervix.
Diagnosis: umbilical cord prolapse.
Emergency low transverse cesarean delivery under general anesthesia. Liveborn girl, Apgar 6 at 1 minute and 8 at 5 minutes, admitted to the NICU for observation.
Postoperative course uncomplicated. Insulin per inpatient protocol, back to home doses with endocrinology. Discharged postoperative day 3.

Diagnoses: term pregnancy, delivered; umbilical cord prolapse; emergency cesarean delivery; type 1 diabetes; hypothyroidism.
Discharge medications: home medications as above.
Follow-up: obstetrics wound check 1-2 weeks; endocrinology 1-2 weeks; primary care.

documents.title: Baby update
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Wanted you to know she came by emergency C-section on the 24th, it was terrifying but we're both ok. She's home with us now. Incision healing, OB checked it last week. Sugars bouncing a bit, endo is on it. I'll set up a postpartum visit once I can drive.

documents.title: Re: Baby update
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: I'm so glad you're both okay. I read the hospital summary; that sounds frightening. Message whenever you're ready and we'll find a time. If you notice any mood changes, pain or redness at the incision, or leg swelling, reach out right away.
